text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: high error/latency spike detected on continuous-batching path (kv-cache pressure) in us-west-2. SLOs impacted — paging oncall @alex. Root metrics: 5xx spike, tail latency > 3s, memory alloc growth on runtime nodes.

alex (oncall): On it. Any initial RCA or correlate with recent deploys?

incident-bot: No deploys in last 15m. Autoscaler activity: several scale-ups then evictions. Metric snippet: `continuous_batch.window_ms` saw an increase in avg queued tokens.

chen (runtime): Looking at runtime logs now. Seeing KV cache eviction storms when large multi-sequence requests hit. Continuous batching config currently: `max_batch_tokens=65536`, `max_num_seqs=32`, `window_ms=50`. Some clients sending huge seqs (long context chat) and causing batch token blowouts -> OOM / GC pressure -> latencies spike.

sasha (eng-sre): Are we seeing hot spots on specific model shards or whole cluster?

chen (runtime): Mostly on nvidia-a100-48 nodes in us-west-2 pool A. Kernel mem stepping up then process restarts. I can push a quick config hotfix to reduce batch size and shorten window. That should stop the blowups immediately.

alex (oncall): Do it. Steps? Keep me posted.

chen (runtime): Plan: 1) Patch runtime config for pool A: `max_batch_tokens=8192`, `max_num_seqs=8`, `window_ms=10` 2) Apply a per-route rate cap for high token routes 3) Disable continuous batching for the most impacted model as fallback.

chen (runtime): Applying config now via admin API: ```
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/api/pools/us-west-2-A/config
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'
  -d '{"continuous_batch":{"max_batch_tokens":8192,"max_num_seqs":8,"window_ms":10}}'
```

deploy-bot: config-update succeeded for pool us-west-2-A @ 1760103589 :white_check_mark:

mira (oncall): Observability — I see p95 latency drop from ~1.8s to ~400ms within 30s of the change. Error rate down. Memory pressure normalized on those nodes. Nice.

customer-support: We're seeing reports from AcmeCorp chat team: intermittent 5-10s responses for ~2% of requests between 14:20-14:30 PT. They've been notified of a degraded experience; will follow up once we confirm mitigation.

kevin (product): Any risk to quality? Do we expect generation truncation because of smaller batches?

chen (runtime): Short-term: slight throughput reduction and higher CPU per-token, but latency SLOs restored. No model quality/regression expected. We'll prioritize more nuanced solutions: adaptive batching, per-tenant token caps, and KV cache eviction policy tuning.

alex (oncall): Handing off to mira for next 2hr watch. mira — please start post-incident timeline and customer impact note. I'll follow up in the morning.

mira (oncall): Taking over. Starting timeline now. Action items recorded: 1) Revert pool config after proper canary (no) — we should not revert until safe. 2) Create a short-lived token limit gate for large requests. 3) Postmortem ticket and follow-up on adaptive batching.

sasha (eng-sre): Quick mitigation note: we also bumped cluster autoscaler min replicas to avoid thrash while we stabilize: `min_replicas` from 3 -> 6 in us-west-2-A.

chen (runtime): Leaving continuous-batching disabled for model: `redwood-internal/xlarge-v1` on pool A as fallback until we roll adaptive change. Command: ```
POST /admin/models/xlarge-v1/flags {"continuous_batching":"off"}
```

incident-bot: STATUS CHANGE: mitigated -> partial (customers impacted but mitigation in place) — monitoring for 30m.

mira (oncall): Customer-impact summary: AcmeCorp ~2% requests > 5s, BetaChatCorp 0.1% errors. No broad data loss. Next steps: PM to coordinate rate-limiting plan, runtime to prototype adaptive batching, SRE to tune autoscaler and eviction heuristics.

kevin (product): I'll take PM for coordinating with customers and drafting the mitigation timeline.

alex (oncall): Marking this as incident-bridge start. I'll add the incident channel and invite stakeholders. Great work everyone. :thumbsup:

mira (oncall): Will produce postmortem draft in incidents repo, linking logs, config diffs, and the exact commands used. Closing paging to alex. Monitoring continues.
